plain.li: [first] A year ago today the {CAMP} went on their way and left {SUBJECT} behind. {A_nameDef} has been out to look at it twice since breakfast.
[years] {YEARS} years since the {CAMP} went on their way. {A_nameDef} still says {WHO}'s name when the day comes round, and wants a walk out to {SUBJECT}.
[about:seeds] The saplings the tree-singers pressed in round their old fire are taller every year. {A_nameDef} wants the colony to walk out and stand in the ring today.
[about:bird] {A_nameDef} took the carved bird down and dusted it this morning. It's the day the hermit left it at the colony's door.

[about:backdrop] The painted castle still stands where the players had their stage, more weathered each year. {A_nameDef} wants the colony out in front of it, standing where they stood for the last act.
[about:sprig] The flowers the mourners set by the gate have come up again. {A_nameDef} said at breakfast whose day it is, in case anyone had forgotten.
[tradition] {NAME}. There's a path worn out to {SUBJECT} now, from all the years of walking it, and {A_nameDef} was first on it this morning.
[winter] Snow on the ground for {NAME}. {A_nameDef} has cleared the path out to {SUBJECT} already.

warm.li: {A_nameDef} still talks about {WHO} as if the camp might come back up the road any day. Today {A_pronoun} wants to go out and stand by {SUBJECT} a while.

blunt.li: {NAME}. {A_nameDef} wants a walk out to {SUBJECT}. It won't take long.

cheerful.li: {A_nameDef} has been up since dawn. It's {NAME}, and {A_pronoun} wants the whole table to come and see how {SUBJECT} is doing.

gloomy.li: {NAME}. {A_nameDef} wonders aloud whether any of the {CAMP} are still on the road, and whether they ever think of this place.

cold.li: {NAME}. {A_nameDef} notes that {SUBJECT} has outlasted the camp by {YEARS} years, and proposes the usual walk.

plain.li: [new] The {CAMP} packed up and went this morning. They left {SUBJECT} behind, and I went out to look at it before anyone else was up.
[new] {WHO} and the rest are gone. {COUNT} days they were here, and now there's {SUBJECT} where their camp stood.
[new,about:seeds] The tree-singers pressed seeds into the ground round their old fire before they left, every other step, singing. I counted the spots twice.
[new,about:bird] There was a carved bird in a crate by the door this morning. The hermit never said goodbye. I think this was it.
[new,about:backdrop] The players left their castle standing where the stage was. Without the actors in front of it, it looks smaller.
[!new,first] A year since the {CAMP} left. We walked out to {SUBJECT} and stood there without saying much, which felt right.
[!new,years] {YEARS} years. {SUBJECT} is still there. I don't know where {WHO} is now.
[!new,tradition] We walked out to {SUBJECT} again, the way we always do on this day. Somebody always tells the story of the camp, and somebody always gets it wrong.

warm.li: [new] They're gone, and I already miss the smoke from their fire. {SUBJECT} will do for remembering them.
[!new] Stood by {SUBJECT} today and told the young ones about {WHO}. They listened better than I expected.

blunt.li: [new] Camp's gone. Left {SUBJECT}. Decent of them.
[!new] Walked out to {SUBJECT}. Walked back. Good day.

cheerful.li: [new] The {CAMP} left us {SUBJECT}! I've already shown it to three people and the dog.
[!new] {NAME}! We all walked out to {SUBJECT} and I swear it's grown, or got more handsome.

gloomy.li: [new] The {CAMP} moved on. People come and go out here, and mostly they don't come back.
[!new] {NAME}. Every year I half expect {SUBJECT} to be gone, and every year it's still there. I don't know why that surprises me.

cold.li: [new] The camp left at dawn, and nothing of ours left with them. {SUBJECT} stays. Fair trade for the wood they burned.
[!new] {NAME}. A walk, an hour. It keeps people in good spirits for little cost.

plain.li: {A_nameDef} and {B_nameDef} tried to remember everything the {CAMP} said on their last night.
{A_nameDef} told {B_nameDef} how {WHO} looked the morning the camp left.
{A_nameDef} and {B_nameDef} argued about whether {SUBJECT} has changed since the camp left.
{A_nameDef} wondered to {B_nameDef} where the {CAMP} are now.
{A_nameDef} told {B_nameDef} about the evenings at the camp's fire, and who sat where.
{NAME} went by without a walk this year. {A_nameDef} went out to {SUBJECT} alone after supper.
No walk out to {SUBJECT} this year. {A_nameDef} mentioned it once at supper and let it drop.

warm.li: {NAME} went by unmarked this year. {A_nameDef} said {WHO} wouldn't have minded.

blunt.li: No walk for {NAME} this year. Too much else to do.

cheerful.li: {NAME} slipped by this year. {A_nameDef} says {SUBJECT} will still be there next time.

gloomy.li: {NAME} passed with no walk. {A_nameDef} thinks the camp is being forgotten, and maybe it is.

cold.li: {NAME} let pass. {SUBJECT} needs no visitors to keep standing.

plain.li: [first] A year ago {SUBJECT} came to an end, and the colony had its part in how. {A_nameDef} remembers the day the word came.
[years] {YEARS} years since {SUBJECT}. {A_nameDef} still tells it the way it happened, starting with the first rider at the gate.
The day {SUBJECT} ended. {A_nameDef} wants it marked, so the newer people know what the colony did that season.
[ws:hunger|ws:drought|ws:scarcity] {SUBJECT} is a year further back, and the stores are full this morning. {A_nameDef} wants a proper supper for it, the kind the colony went without that season.
[ws:war|ws:levy|ws:sellswords] The day {SUBJECT} ended. {A_nameDef} would like the colony to walk out to the gate together, where the riders used to come in.
[ws:sickness] The day {SUBJECT} burned itself out. {A_nameDef} wants a walk to the gate and a word for the ones who nursed and the ones who didn't get up again.
[ws:fair|ws:trade|ws:songs] The anniversary of {SUBJECT}. {A_nameDef} remembers the noise and the colors, and wants a day of it back.
[tradition] {NAME}, kept so many years now that the newest people think it's an old custom of the land.

warm.li: {NAME}. {A_nameDef} still thinks of the people of {WHO} on this day, and hopes they think of the colony.

blunt.li: {NAME}. {A_nameDef} wants it kept. That season was hard enough to earn it.

cheerful.li: {NAME}! {A_nameDef} says it's the one day a year the colony gets to be proud of itself out loud.

gloomy.li: {NAME}. {A_nameDef} counts the faces that were here for {SUBJECT} and finds fewer every year.

cold.li: {NAME}. {A_nameDef} points out that what the colony did then is why {WHO} still deal fairly with it.

plain.li: [new] Word came today that {SUBJECT} is over. We did our part. I don't know yet if it was enough.
[new] {SUBJECT} is done with. I slept through the night for the first time in a while.
[new,ws:hunger|ws:drought|ws:scarcity] The hungry season is over. I keep looking at the stores as if they might empty again overnight.
[new,ws:war|ws:levy] The fighting is over, or this round of it is. The road is quiet again.
[!new,first] A year since {SUBJECT}. We marked it, and the newcomers asked a lot of questions.
[!new,years] {YEARS} years since {SUBJECT}. Funny which parts I remember: the smell of the smoke, not the dates.
[!new,tradition] We kept the day of {SUBJECT} the way it's always kept. I could tell the story in my sleep.

warm.li: [new] {SUBJECT} is over, and the people of {WHO} sent word of thanks. I read it twice.
[!new] Remembered {SUBJECT} today with the ones who were here for it. We held on to each other that season.

blunt.li: [!new] Day of {SUBJECT}. Marked it. Back to work tomorrow.

cheerful.li: [new] It's over! {SUBJECT} is finished and we're still standing, and so are the people of {WHO}.
[!new] We kept the day of {SUBJECT} and I told the best version of the story yet.

gloomy.li: [new] {SUBJECT} has ended. There'll be another along to take its place before long.
[!new] The day of {SUBJECT}. I thought about the ones it took, out there, who aren't in anyone's calendar.

cold.li: [new] {SUBJECT} has ended. What we gave was worth what we got for it, on balance.
[!new] The day of {SUBJECT}. Remembering it keeps people careful, which is useful.

plain.li: {A_nameDef} told {B_nameDef} what the colony did during {SUBJECT}, and what it nearly did instead.
{A_nameDef} and {B_nameDef} remembered the season of {SUBJECT}.
{A_nameDef} asked {B_nameDef} whether the people of {WHO} still remember what the colony did.
{A_nameDef} told {B_nameDef} the story of {SUBJECT}, bigger than last year.
The day of {SUBJECT} went by unmarked this year. {A_nameDef} noticed, and said nothing.
{NAME} went unkept this year. {A_nameDef} told the story of it to one listener over supper instead.

warm.li: {NAME} passed without a word. {A_nameDef} raised a cup to it alone, which may be enough.

blunt.li: {NAME} let go this year. There wasn't time.

cheerful.li: {NAME} slipped past this year. {A_nameDef} says the story keeps, and it'll be twice as good next year.

gloomy.li: {NAME} passed unmarked. A few more years like this and the newer people won't know what it was.

cold.li: {NAME} let pass. The colony has more pressing matters than an old season.

plain.li: Today is the {WHO}, a holy day of {SUBJECT}. {A_nameDef} has been up since before dawn getting ready.
[years] The {WHO} has come round again. {A_nameDef} remembers how it was kept in the colony's first years, with far fewer people.
[devout] {A_nameDef} fasted yesterday for the {WHO}, as {SUBJECT} asks of the devout, and wants the day kept properly.
[tradition] The {WHO}. The colony keeps it without being asked now; {A_nameDef} found the altar swept before anyone was up.
[winter] The {WHO} falls in the cold this year as every year. {A_nameDef} says the faithful have kept it in worse weather.

warm.li: The {WHO}. {A_nameDef} says it's the one day a year {SUBJECT} asks nothing hard of anyone, only that they come.

cheerful.li: The {WHO}! {A_nameDef} has been humming the old hymns since breakfast.

gloomy.li: The {WHO}. {A_nameDef} hopes {SUBJECT} is watching, given the year the colony has had.

cold.li: The {WHO}. {A_nameDef} observes that the faithful work better after it, and recommends keeping it.

plain.li: The {WHO}. We kept it, and for an evening the colony felt like it had one heart.
[first] Our first {WHO} kept the way {SUBJECT} keeps it. I didn't know all the words. Next year I will.
[years] Another {WHO}. The words come easier every year, and mean more.
[tradition] The {WHO}, kept as it always is here. The children know the hymns better than I do.

warm.li: The {WHO}. I held the hand of the person next to me through the whole of the last hymn.
A holy day of {SUBJECT}. I felt close to the others, even the ones I argue with.

cheerful.li: The {WHO}! I sang too loudly and the cook sang louder.
Holy day today, and the best supper of the season after it.

gloomy.li: The {WHO}. I prayed for the ones we've lost this year. The list was longer than I wanted.
A holy day. I'm not sure {SUBJECT} hears us out here, but I said the words anyway.

cold.li: The {WHO}. It holds the faithful together, and that holds the colony together.
Holy day kept. The devout are calmer for it.

plain.li: {A_nameDef} told {B_nameDef} what the {WHO} means to the followers of {SUBJECT}.
{A_nameDef} and {B_nameDef} went over the words for the {WHO} together.
{A_nameDef} asked {B_nameDef} how the {WHO} was kept where {B_pronoun} grew up.
{A_nameDef} and {B_nameDef} talked about the last {WHO}, and who wasn't there for it this year.
The {WHO} went by without the colony keeping it. {A_nameDef} said the words alone, at dusk.
No {WHO} this year. {A_nameDef} lit a candle for it anyway and didn't tell anyone.

warm.li: The {WHO} passed unkept. {A_nameDef} says {SUBJECT} is patient, and next year will do.

blunt.li: No {WHO} this year. {A_nameDef} didn't like it.

cheerful.li: The {WHO} slipped past this year. {A_nameDef} hummed the hymns over the washing, which {A_pronoun} says counts.

gloomy.li: The {WHO} went unkept. {A_nameDef} wonders what else the colony is letting go of.

cold.li: The {WHO} let pass. The devout will remember it.

plain.li: [first] A year ago today {A_nameDef} came home after {COUNT} days held by {WHO}. {A_nameDef} would rather not talk about those days, but wants the colony at one table tonight.
[years] {YEARS} years since {A_nameDef} was brought home. The others want a supper for it; {A_nameDef} says {A_pronoun}'ll only come if there's no speech.
The day {A_nameDef} came home. Someone has already hung a lamp in the gate, the way one hung there every night {A_pronoun} was gone.
[tradition] {NAME}. Kept every year now. {A_nameDef} still looks embarrassed by it, and still turns up.

warm.li: {NAME}. {A_nameDef} spent the morning thanking the ones who went to fetch {A_objective}, one at a time.

blunt.li: {NAME}. {A_nameDef} is glad to be here. That's all {A_pronoun} will say about it.

cheerful.li: {NAME}! {A_nameDef} is home and has been for a whole year, and wants a feast to prove it.

gloomy.li: {NAME}. {A_nameDef} hasn't slept well this week. The day brings it all back.

cold.li: {NAME}. {A_nameDef} notes that {WHO} lost a prisoner that day and have never come for {A_objective} again.

plain.li: [new,!friend] Home. {COUNT} days with {WHO}, and I'm home. My own bed smells of dust and I don't care.
[new,!friend] They brought me home today. I kept waking in the night to make sure it was true.
[new,friend] {OTHER_nameDef} is home. Thinner, quieter, home. I made {OTHER_objective} eat twice before {OTHER_pronoun} slept.
[!new,first,!friend] A year since I came home. They laid the long table. I sat with my back to the wall, the way I've sat ever since.
[!new,years,!friend] {YEARS} years home now. Some nights it feels longer, some nights like last week.
[!new,tradition,!friend] My homecoming again. They make a fuss and I let them. It's become theirs as much as mine.
[!new,friend] {NAME}. We laid the long table, and I watched the gate out of habit, the way I did every night of those {COUNT} days.
[!new,friend,years] {YEARS} years since we brought them home. I still remember the weight of the lamp I hung in the gate.

warm.li: [new,!friend] They all came to the gate, even the ones I hardly talk to. I didn't know they would.
[new,friend] {OTHER_nameDef} is back with us. I didn't let go of {OTHER_possessive} hand for a long time.
[!new,!friend] The day I came home. I thanked each of them again. They pretended it was nothing.

blunt.li: [!new] Homecoming supper. Ate well. Didn't talk about the rest.

cheerful.li: [new,!friend] I'm home! I hugged the door frame. I'd hug the walls if they'd let me.
[new,friend] {OTHER_nameDef} is home and I'm so glad I could sing.
[!new,!friend] My homecoming day! The cook made my favorite, without being asked.

gloomy.li: [new,!friend] I'm home. Part of me is still there, with {WHO}, waiting for the door.
[new,friend] {OTHER_nameDef} came home today, but not all of {OTHER_objective} did. Not yet.
[!new,!friend] The day I came home. I spent most of it remembering why I needed to.

cold.li: [new,!friend] Returned after {COUNT} days. I learned a good deal about {WHO}'s camp. It may be useful.
[new,friend] {OTHER_nameDef} is back, and still fit to work. A good outcome.
[!new,!friend] My homecoming. The colony likes the day more than I do.

plain.li: {A_nameDef} told {B_nameDef} about the night {A_pronoun} was brought home.
{A_nameDef} and {B_nameDef} talked about the {COUNT} days with {WHO}, as far as {A_nameDef} would go.
{A_nameDef} thanked {B_nameDef} again for the day {A_pronoun} came home.
{A_nameDef} told {B_nameDef} what {A_pronoun} missed most while {A_pronoun} was gone.
{NAME} went by without a supper this year. {A_nameDef} said {A_pronoun} preferred it that way.
No homecoming supper for {A_nameDef} this year. {A_pronoun} sat by the gate a while at dusk instead.

warm.li: {NAME} went by without a supper this year. {A_nameDef} says being home is enough.

blunt.li: No fuss for {NAME} this year. {A_nameDef} didn't want one.

cheerful.li: {NAME} slipped by this year. {A_nameDef} says every day home is a homecoming anyway.

gloomy.li: {NAME} went unmarked. {A_nameDef} noticed, and kept to {A_possessive} room all evening.

cold.li: {NAME} let pass. {A_nameDef} has other days to think about.

plain.li: {NAME}. {A_nameDef} would like the colony to walk out together and stand a while where it belongs.
[first] The first {NAME} since it happened. {A_nameDef} asks the colony to walk out with {A_objective} this afternoon.
[years] {YEARS} years since {NAME} first came. {A_nameDef} wants the walk out made again, at the same easy pace as the first time.
[tradition] {NAME}, and the walk out that goes with it. People were lacing their boots before {A_nameDef} said a word.

warm.li: {NAME}. {A_nameDef} says a walk together is the best way to keep a day like this.

blunt.li: {NAME}. A walk out and back. {A_nameDef} will lead.

cheerful.li: {NAME}! {A_nameDef} has picked the long way round, because it's prettier.

gloomy.li: {NAME}. {A_nameDef} wants a walk. A quiet one.

cold.li: {NAME}. {A_nameDef} proposes a walk: an hour away from the work, and back before dark.

plain.li: {NAME}. We walked out together and stood there a while, and took the long way back.
[years] {NAME}, the walk out again. Same path, a few different faces.
[tradition] The walk for {NAME}, as always. I could do it with my eyes shut.

warm.li: {NAME}. On the way back somebody took my arm without saying anything.

cheerful.li: {NAME}! We went the long way and picked berries on the way home.

gloomy.li: {NAME}. A long quiet walk. I thought about more than I meant to.

cold.li: {NAME}. An hour's walk. People came back steadier for it.

plain.li: {A_nameDef} and {B_nameDef} talked about {NAME} on the walk back.
{A_nameDef} told {B_nameDef} why {NAME} is worth walking out for.
{A_nameDef} and {B_nameDef} walked at the back and talked about old times.
